BIOS Backup SRAM

Use this 32 KiB battery-backed SRAM for BIOS settings and other retained state. Return to the main page.

Document status
Revision 1.0 pre-layout design; timing and retention require board measurements
Memory map
Frozen revision 2.3, I/O slot 13
Parts
One HM62256ALP-10SL, one DS1210+ in PDIP, and a separate CR2032 in a BA2032 holder
Capacity
32,768 bytes; offset zero is the BIOS diagnostic byte
Access
Supervisor CPU byte reads and writes on D7..D0; no DMA access

1. Addressing

The memory map assigns $FA0000-$FBFFFF to this subsystem. Use MOVE.B for reads and writes. Bus A1..A15 select SRAM A0..A14; A16 has no connection to the local decoder. 

BIOS byte offset N = 0..32767
canonical address = $FA0001 + 2*N
mirror address    = $FB0001 + 2*N
Slot 13 address contract
Addresses Meaning
$FA0001, mirror $FB0001 Diagnostic byte, offset zero
Odd addresses $FA0003-$FAFFFF 32,767 bytes available to BIOS retained records
Odd addresses $FB0003-$FBFFFF Mirrors of those same bytes, not extra storage
Even-byte or word accesses No SRAM selection or local completion; motherboard timeout reports a bus error

The qualified IO13_n comes from U_IO_HIGH /Y5, pin 10. The existing protection and ownership gates exclude user, CPU-space, and DMA cycles. Slot 14 stays reserved. BIOS stacks, vectors, and working state remain in physical DRAM $000000-$01FFFF. The page unit cannot map this SRAM into a user context.

2. Memory and Battery Wiring

Fit U_BSRAM as the HM62256ALP-10SL, a 100 ns, 600-mil 28-pin DIP. Use the L-SL retention limits from HM62256A, pages 1-2 and 11.

U_BSRAM pin connections
Pin(s) SRAM signal(s) Connection, in matching order
10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3 A0..A7 Bus A1..A8
25, 24, 21, 23, 2, 26, 1 A8..A14 Bus A9..A15
11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 I/O0..I/O7 Bus D0..D7
20 /CS BSRAM_CEO_n from DS1210 pin 6; no other load or pull resistor
22 /OE BSRAM_OE_n
27 /WE BSRAM_WE_n
28 VCC BSRAM_VCC from DS1210 pin 1; 100 nF ceramic to ground at this pin
14 VSS Ground
U_BSRAM_NV, DS1210+ 8-pin PDIP connections
Pin Signal Connection
1 VCCO BSRAM_VCC, SRAM supply only
2 VBAT1 BT_BSRAM CR2032 positive terminal
3 TOL Ground, 5% supply tolerance selection
4 GND Ground, shared with cell negative terminal
5 /CE BSRAM_CE_n; 10 kohm pull-up to switched +5 V
6 /CEO BSRAM_CEO_n, SRAM pin 20 only
7 VBAT2 Ground, unused battery input
8 VCCI Switched motherboard +5 V; 100 nF ceramic to ground

Connect the BA2032 holder contacts by their positive and negative markings. Keep BT_BSRAM separate from BT_RTC. Fit no charging path, series diode, or external load on the battery net. Power the clock buffer and interface gates from switched +5 V.

3. Bus Qualification

Use the shared, buffered bus controls described in Bus and Address Decode. R_W is the local spelling of the shared R/W net; 1 means read. Require LDS_n = 0 and UDS_n = 1; a word cycle must not write its lower byte. 

UDS_ACTIVE       = NOT UDS_n
RESET_ACTIVE     = NOT RESET_n
WRITE_ACTIVE     = NOT R_W
BSRAM_LANE_n     = IO13_n OR LDS_n
BSRAM_BLOCK      = UDS_ACTIVE OR RESET_ACTIVE
BSRAM_SELECT_n   = BSRAM_LANE_n OR BSRAM_BLOCK
BSRAM_REQ_n      = BSRAM_SELECT_n OR AS_n
BSRAM_ACTIVE     = NOT BSRAM_REQ_n
BSRAM_CE_n       = BSRAM_REQ_n OR Q2_n
BSRAM_OE_n       = BSRAM_CE_n OR WRITE_ACTIVE
BSRAM_WRITE_n    = BSRAM_CE_n OR R_W
BSRAM_WE_n       = LDS_n OR BSRAM_WRITE_n

The final LDS term ends a write through one AHCT gate after LDS rises. The SRAM ends a write on the first rising edge of /WE or /CS. Do not rely on the DS1210 propagation delay to meet write-data hold. Gate DS1210 /CE with Q2_n so a brief lane-strobe mismatch cannot select SRAM before the second delay stage. Check the glitch and clear-path budget below during word cycles before accepting this pre-layout circuit.

Interface gate assignment
Package / part Input pins → output pin: signals
U_BSRAM_INV, SN74HCT04N 1 → 2: UDS_n → UDS_ACTIVE; 3 → 4: RESET_n → RESET_ACTIVE; 5 → 6: R_W → WRITE_ACTIVE; 9 → 8: BSRAM_REQ_n → BSRAM_ACTIVE
U_BSRAM_OR_A, SN74AHCT32N 1,2 → 3: IO13_n, LDS_n → BSRAM_LANE_n; 4,5 → 6: UDS_ACTIVE, RESET_ACTIVE → BSRAM_BLOCK; 9,10 → 8: BSRAM_LANE_n, BSRAM_BLOCK → BSRAM_SELECT_n; 12,13 → 11: BSRAM_SELECT_n, AS_n → BSRAM_REQ_n
U_BSRAM_OR_B, SN74AHCT32N 1,2 → 3: BSRAM_CE_n, WRITE_ACTIVE → BSRAM_OE_n; 4,5 → 6: BSRAM_CE_n, R_W → BSRAM_WRITE_n; 9,10 → 8: BSRAM_REQ_n, Q4_n → BSRAM_ACK_BLOCK_n; 12,13 → 11: AS_n, BSRAM_ACK_BLOCK_n → BSRAM_DTACK_n
U_BSRAM_OR_C, SN74AHCT32N 1,2 → 3: LDS_n, BSRAM_WRITE_n → BSRAM_WE_n; 4,5 → 6: BSRAM_REQ_n, Q2_n → BSRAM_CE_n

Ground U_BSRAM_INV inputs 11 and 13; leave outputs 10 and 12 open. Ground U_BSRAM_OR_C inputs 9, 10, 12, and 13; leave outputs 8 and 11 open. These 14-pin packages use pin 14 for +5 V and pin 7 for ground, with one 100 nF ceramic per package.

4. Clock and Completion

Add U_BSRAM_CLK_BUF, a CD74ACT244E. Ground enable pins 1 and 19, feed pin 2 from DRAM_CLK_10, and use pin 18 as BSRAM_CLK_ROOT. Feed that root to pins 4 and 6. Pin 16 supplies BSRAM_CLK; pin 14 supplies STARTUP_CLK_10 to U_STARTUP_DIV pin 10, replacing its former DRAM_CLK_10 connection. Ground unused inputs 8, 11, 13, 15, and 17; leave outputs 12, 9, 7, 5, and 3 open. Pins 20 and 10 connect to +5 V and ground, with a 100 nF bypass capacitor. The existing clock buffer has no spare channel.

Use two SN74AHCT74N packages, U_BSRAM_DELAY_A and U_BSRAM_DELAY_B, for a four-stage request delay. Feed pins 3 and 11 of both packages from BSRAM_CLK; feed clear pins 1 and 13 from BSRAM_ACTIVE. Tie preset pins 4 and 10 high. Connect pin 14 to +5 V and pin 7 to ground, with one 100 nF capacitor per package.

Delay data connections
Stage D input Q output / next connection
Q1 Delay A pin 2: +5 V Delay A pin 5 → Delay A pin 12
Q2 Delay A pin 12: Q1 Delay A pin 9 → Delay B pin 2; pin 8 is Q2_n → U_BSRAM_OR_C pin 5
Q3 Delay B pin 2: Q2 Delay B pin 5 → Delay B pin 12
Q4 Delay B pin 12: Q3 Delay B pin 8: Q4_n → U_BSRAM_OR_B pin 10; pin 9 open

Leave Delay A pin 6 and Delay B pin 6 open.

While BSRAM_ACTIVE = 0: Q1 = Q2 = Q3 = Q4 = 0
On each rising BSRAM_CLK edge while BSRAM_ACTIVE = 1:
  Q1 <- 1
  Q2 <- Q1
  Q3 <- Q2
  Q4 <- Q3

BSRAM_ACK_BLOCK_n = BSRAM_REQ_n OR Q4_n
BSRAM_DTACK_n     = AS_n OR BSRAM_ACK_BLOCK_n
DTACK_GROUP3_n    = IDE_DTACK_n AND DMAC_DTACK_n AND BSRAM_DTACK_n AND 1

Use old stage values for each clock edge. Route BSRAM_DTACK_n to U_DTACK_C gate 1 pin 4, replacing its +5 V tie. Keep pin 1 as IDE_DTACK_n, pin 2 as DMAC_DTACK_n, pin 5 high, and pin 6 as DTACK_GROUP3_n. Retain the final timeout mask.

Generate completion from the bus request, not DS1210 /CEO. The BIOS must finish a probe cycle even if the DS1210 inhibits SRAM access. The SRAM has no ready or battery-status output. AS high releases completion through the final OR gate; request removal clears all stages. Reset suppresses requests and clears the delay.

5. Timing and Loading

Use the MC68EC000 10 MHz limits in M68000 User's Manual, section 10.14, the HM62256A -10 column, pages 6-11, and the DS1210, pages 4-6. Calculations below start at the named local net, after motherboard decode. They exclude routing, master-buffer skew, and loading above the datasheet test conditions.

Calculated timing budget at 10 MHz
Check Calculation / requirement
Read data after BSRAM_CE_n falls DS1210 /CE delay 20 ns + SRAM /CS access 100 ns = 120 ns; also require address access 100 ns and /OE access 50 ns
Normal delay after Q1 captures Q4 follows Q1 by three periods. Selection begins after Q2; two periods leave 199.980 - 10 ns Q2 CLK-to-Q - 9 ns select gate - 120 ns memory path = 60.980 ns before the Q4 clock
Stage setup margin 99.990 - 10 ns CLK-to-Q - 5 ns setup = 84.990 ns for skew and interconnect
Q4 clock to CPU completion 10 ns + two AHCT32 gates at 9 ns + two F21 gates at 7 ns + F32 at 8.5 ns = 50.5 ns
AS release to CPU completion release 9 + 7 + 7 + 8.5 = 31.5 ns from shared AS; 78.5 ns remains within CPU parameter #28, before master-buffer and route delays
Delay clear from shared AS high 9 ns request gate + 25 ns HCT04 + 13 ns clear-to-Q = 47 ns; 58 ns remains within the 105 ns inactive interval
Read output release from shared AS high 9 + 9 + 9 ns through request, /CE, and /OE gates + 35 ns SRAM tOHZ = 62 ns, against CPU #29A maximum 150 ns
Write requirements tWC 100 ns, tCW 80 ns, tWP 60 ns, tDW 40 ns; address setup, write recovery, and data hold are each 0 ns minimum
Write-window budget 199.980 - 10 - 9 - 20 = 160.980 ns from latest /CS assertion to earliest Q4 clock, giving 80.980 ns above tCW and 100.980 ns above tWP before completion and CPU release
Write-data hold CPU #25 gives 30 ns at 10 MHz; one 9 ns LDS-to-/WE gate leaves 21 ns for relative control/data buffer and route delay

For word-cycle glitch rejection, require any false BSRAM_REQ_n low pulse plus the 25 ns inverter and 13 ns clear-to-Q path to stay below one 99.990 ns clock period, including routing and skew. This keeps Q1 clear before Q2 can select memory. Measure that bound at Q1/Q2 with the earliest and latest lane strobes; a truth table alone does not prove it. Check address-valid and /OE timing alongside /CS timing. For reads, require data at least 5 ns before the CPU sample edge. For writes, the CPU presents data at least 30 ns before LDS assertion (#26) and holds it throughout wait states. The delayed completion supplies write setup margin, but the final /WE edge must still precede loss of valid data at the SRAM pins.

The request and clear release can violate stage-1 setup or recovery. As with the ROM delay, the later stages provide settling time; the arithmetic does not establish a metastability failure rate. Measure recovery, clock skew, CPU parameter #28A, and back-to-back cycles.

Net Added load / drive check
Bus A1..A15 One SRAM input per line: 6 pF and 1 uA maximum
Bus D0..D7 One SRAM I/O per line: 8 pF and 1 uA leakage maximum while deselected
SRAM data outputs VOH 2.4 V at -1 mA; VOL 0.4 V at 2.1 mA. Sum existing bus receiver loads and verify the complete read path at these drive limits
IO13_n / UDS_n / RESET_n One AHCT32 / one HCT04 / one HCT04 input, respectively; budget 10 pF and 1 uA per input
LDS_n / AS_n / R_W Two AHCT32 / two AHCT32 / one HCT04 plus one AHCT32 input, respectively; budget 20 pF and 2 uA per net
DRAM_CLK_10 Replace the startup-counter input with one ACT244 input, 10 pF/1 uA maximum. Four receivers remain: refresh counter, ROM buffer, interrupt buffer, and SRAM root buffer; at most 40 pF before routing
BSRAM_CLK_ROOT / STARTUP_CLK_10 Two ACT244 inputs / one HCT4040 clock input: up to 20 pF / 10 pF before routing. The startup divider retains 10 MHz with two added buffer delays; check reset recovery
BSRAM_CLK Four AHCT74 clock inputs, up to 40 pF; retain 10 pF for routing within a 50 pF timing load
BSRAM_ACTIVE Four clear inputs: up to 40 pF; retain 10 pF for routing within a 50 pF timing load
BSRAM_REQ_n Two AHCT32 inputs and one HCT04 input: up to 30 pF before routing
BSRAM_CE_n Two AHCT32 inputs and DS1210 /CE: up to 25 pF plus a 10 kohm pull-up (0.5 mA at 5 V when low)
BSRAM_CEO_n One SRAM /CS input, 6 pF and 1 uA. DS1210 drive is -1 mA high, 4 mA low; no FAST input or other powered-down load on this net
BSRAM_DTACK_n One F21 input: 20 uA high, 0.6 mA low; AHCT32 +/-8 mA drive gives at least 13x low-state current margin

The new buffer adds no direct CPU_CLK_10 load. Use the stated input maxima when updating the bus and clock loading audits. SRAM read access uses the manufacturer's 100 pF output test load; high-impedance timing uses its separate 5 pF condition. Include probe capacitance in board measurements.

6. Power and Retention

With TOL grounded, the DS1210 trip range is 4.50-4.74 V. At normal input voltage it guarantees VCCO at least VCCI - 0.2 V; a 4.75 V input therefore leaves at least 4.55 V at SRAM, above the SRAM's 4.5 V operating minimum. Do not select the 10% trip option.

The SRAM draws at most 50 mA at its minimum -10 cycle time, below the DS1210's 80 mA average output rating before I/O loads. The SRAM's 50 mA specification excludes output current; include the actual data-bus source current and require the total VCCO load to stay below 80 mA. Add the DS1210's 5 mA maximum operating current and the interface logic to the switched +5 V budget. Use 55 mA as the memory/controller subtotal, not the complete subsystem current. Calculate logic switching current from the cited parts' Cpd and routed loads; measure the assembled branch under continuous reads and writes. A 40 pF clock load at 5 V and 10 MHz alone requires about 2 mA of dynamic supply current.

For the L-SL SRAM, retention current at 3 V is 0.2 uA typical, 3 uA maximum over 0-40 C, and 10 uA maximum over 0-70 C. Adding the DS1210's 0.1 uA maximum battery current gives 3.1 uA and 10.1 uA budgets, before holder, capacitor, and PCB leakage. Both fit below its 50 uA battery-mode output rating. Use the chosen cell's rated capacity and discharge curve for a life estimate; do not promise a service interval from typical SRAM current.

The SRAM requires at least 2.0 V for retention. The DS1210 specifies VCCO at least VBAT - 0.3 V under its backup-load condition, so a 2.3 V cell is the minimum arithmetic input for guaranteed 2.0 V SRAM power. Allow replacement margin above that value. Its 2.0 V battery-warning threshold does not prove adequate retention voltage.

The DS1210 holds /CEO high near the retained supply during backup. Follow the SRAM requirement /CS >= VCC - 0.2 V. The SRAM retention note permits other inputs to float while /CS controls retention; keep them free of negative voltage and prevent other circuits from loading VCCO or /CEO. Do not add battery-powered pull-ups to the bus.

On power failure, the DS1210 lets an active enable cycle finish before write protection. Its /CE low pulse must not exceed 1.5 us. A normal four-stage request needs about 0.3-0.4 us plus logic and CPU termination, so use 1.0 us as the assembled-board acceptance ceiling for normal /CE pulses. The motherboard timeout is not a substitute for this limit. Clock stoppage or a held bus request can exceed it; this circuit provides no independent pulse limiter.

Check the power-down waveform against DS1210 Figure 6: at least 300 us through the specified 4.75-to-4.5 V interval and at least 10 us from 4.5 V to the battery crossover. Check /CEO and SRAM voltage together. The worst-case trip point and switch drop do not prove valid active writes throughout a brownout. BIOS record integrity checks must reject an interrupted or invalid update.

Allow 125 ms after the supply exceeds the DS1210's rising trip threshold before the first SRAM request. The motherboard's 250 ms reset starts at the DS1233 threshold, which need not match the DS1210 threshold. Require a stable valid +5 V rail at reset release and a BIOS delay of at least 150 ms after that release before SRAM access. A warm reset may use the same delay. The DS1210 has no reset input; CPU reset does not erase SRAM or restart its battery test.

A newly attached battery stays behind the DS1210 freshness seal until VCCI has exceeded the selected trip threshold and then fallen below the battery voltage. Complete a powered commissioning cycle before testing off-power retention.

7. BIOS Requirements

Reserve physical SRAM offset zero at $FA0001 for a diagnostic. After the startup delay, make these the first accesses to the SRAM since power-up, before any scan, checksum, or debugger read. Use volatile byte accesses in the order below; keep other firmware paths out of the SRAM during the probe.

  1. Read the diagnostic byte into old.
  2. Write old XOR $FF to the diagnostic byte.
  3. Read it again and compare with old XOR $FF.

The DS1210 inhibits the second memory cycle after power-up if it detects a battery below 2.0 V. With a retained readable byte, that inhibits the test write and causes a mismatch. No restore is needed: this byte belongs to the diagnostic, not a settings record. A mismatch means the BIOS must distrust retention; it is not a calibrated battery measurement. Open-bus values, missing SRAM, or an invalid supply can also affect this test. A match cannot prove battery health, particularly after a warm reset or prior SRAM access.

Validate retained records with a format/version check and checksum or CRC before using their contents. Use defaults after a failed diagnostic or invalid record, and preserve valid records across resets. Use a commit marker or alternate copy when implementing multi-byte updates so an interrupted write cannot pass as a complete record. Define the record layout and BIOS service API with the future BIOS source; this document assigns no additional record addresses.

Exclude slot 13 from DRAM clearing, destructive boot memory tests, program allocators, and DMA buffers. BIOS range validation must reject caller pointers into it. Access persistent settings through checked BIOS services. Never use the mirrored half as another allocation.

8. Components and Layout

Subsystem components
Quantity Part Use
1 HM62256ALP-10SL U_BSRAM, DIP-28, 600 mil
1 DS1210+ U_BSRAM_NV, DIP-8, 300 mil
1 each CR2032 and MPD BA2032 BT_BSRAM and through-hole holder
3 SN74AHCT32N U_BSRAM_OR_A, B, C
1 SN74HCT04N U_BSRAM_INV
2 SN74AHCT74N U_BSRAM_DELAY_A, B
1 CD74ACT244E U_BSRAM_CLK_BUF
9 100 nF ceramic, 10 V or higher One per IC; only the SRAM capacitor uses BSRAM_VCC
1 10 kohm, 5%, 1/8 W DS1210 /CE pull-up to switched +5 V

Place the DS1210 beside SRAM pins 20 and 28. Keep VCCO, /CEO, and battery traces short and clean of flux residue. Put the holder where a user can replace the cell without disturbing the memory wiring. Label cell polarity and distinguish BT_BSRAM from BT_RTC.

Place the clock buffer beside the delay packages. Route the direct LDS-to-/WE path without extra gates and keep control/data skew within the hold budget. Provide probe access to VCCI, BSRAM_VCC, /CE, /CEO, /WE, and BSRAM_DTACK_n. Use a high-impedance probe for retention measurements; a meter or probe can dominate the battery load.

9. Acceptance Checks

  • Verify offset 0 and 32767, each address bit, and both mirrors. Confirm that changing one byte leaves adjacent SRAM bytes intact.
  • Exercise even-byte, word, user, DMA, and CPU-space cycles. Require inactive /CS and /WE and no BSRAM_DTACK_n. Sweep lane and decode skew to detect transient selection during a word cycle.
  • Measure read setup, write width/setup/hold, output release, and CPU completion assertion/release. Test back-to-back read/write cycles and reset or aborted requests at each delay stage.
  • Measure the complete data-bus load, DRAM_CLK_10 and BSRAM_CLK loads, clear-net capacitance, and shortest inactive interval. Resolve any exceeded timing-test load before layout acceptance.
  • Measure normal /CE pulses below 1.0 us and verify the DS1210 1.5 us requirement during power removal. Test power loss during writes at several phases and check surrounding records for damage.
  • Check startup delay from the DS1210 threshold crossing, slow ramps, relay power-off slew, brownout, and warm reset. Confirm that firmware keeps SRAM untouched until the diagnostic probe.
  • With a current-limited battery simulator, test a fresh cell, warning-level voltage, and absent battery. Confirm defaults after invalid records and verify the inhibited second-cycle behavior.
  • After commissioning, write a test pattern, remove main power, measure retained voltage and current, then restore power and compare the pattern excluding the diagnostic byte. Check both temperature-range current budgets and the separate RTC supply.

These are board acceptance requirements, not reported measurements. The repository contains design documentation, not a board schematic or BIOS implementation for this subsystem.
